objectives: LO 8.1.1: Evaluate MPT assumptions, indifference curves, and the efficient frontier
LO 8.2.1: Analyze capital market theory, the CML, CAPM, and the SML
LO 8.3.1: Identify the weak, semistrong, and strong forms of the EMH
LO 8.3.2: Appraise how the EMH relates to technical, fundamental, active/passive, and foreign investing
LO 8.4.1: Identify the components of an investment policy statement
LO 8.5.1: Judge which investments look attractive across interest-rate and economic cycles
LO 8.5.2: Critique strategic, tactical, core-and-satellite, and other allocation methods
LO 8.6.1: Evaluate how clients and planners manage crisis events with severe financial consequences
synthesis: Module 8 turns the risk and return tools from earlier modules into a portfolio process: MPT and CAPM say how much return a given risk deserves, the EMH says whether paying for active management is worth it, and the IPS writes those choices down as a client's policy. Asset allocation then implements that policy across economic cycles, and the crisis section tests whether the client can stick with it when markets break.

example.title: Should Nora buy this fund? (CAPM decision)
example.html:
Nora requires 8% from a new equity fund. The fund's beta is 1.1, T-bills yield 3.5%, and the market is expected to return 8.5%.

  1. Market risk premium = 8.5% − 3.5% = 5.0%
  2. Stock risk premium = 5.0% × 1.1 = 5.5%
  3. CAPM expected return = 3.5% + 5.5% = 9.0%
  4. 9.0% ≥ 8% required → acceptable on a risk-adjusted basis

Check: a beta-0.8 fund would give 3.5% + 5.0% × 0.8 = 7.5%, below her 8% requirement → pass.

keyNumbers: r = a<sub>0</sub> + b<sub>1</sub>F<sub>1</sub> + … + b<sub>n</sub>F<sub>n</sub> + e (4 primary factors)
10–15 large caps (some studies 20–40); ~2× as many small/mid caps; 4–7 asset classes
>90% of return variability from asset allocation
Money needed within ~5 years stays out of stocks
Earnings growth ~15%+/yr, low payout, high P/E, higher beta
mustKnow: Optimal portfolio = tangency of the highest indifference curve with the efficient frontier; steeper curve = more risk averse
CML uses standard deviation (efficient portfolios); SML uses beta (any security); above SML = undervalued
Weak form: fundamental + inside info can win; semistrong: inside info only; strong: nothing; technical analysis never
IPS: return and risk objectives plus liquidity, time horizon, legal, tax, unique circumstances, permitted/excluded investments
Strategic = long-term mix + rebalancing; TAA = contrarian market timing; core-and-satellite = strategic core + tactical satellite
Crisis: ignore noise, watch incremental change, rewrite the IPS for discontinuous change; usually take no action when a client wants cash
traps: Stock risk premium is (r<sub>m</sub> − r<sub>f</sub>)β, not r<sub>m</sub>β and not the full required return
Inflation shifts the SML in parallel; changing risk aversion changes its slope
There is no semiweak form of the EMH
Exchange fund (diversify, keep value, defer gains) is not an exchange-traded fund
tips: For any CAPM decision, compute the required return first, then compare it with the forecast or the client's hurdle
Tie EMH questions to the information set: past prices → public → private
